statement: Global Hunger increases by 0.01 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
Hunger enters warning above 80 and dying above 99.9.
While Hunger is dying, Player Health is reduced by 0.1 per second.
Global Thirst increases by 0.02 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
Thirst warns above 80; above 99.9 the dying state reduces Health by 0.1 per second.
Global Fatigue increases by 0.02 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
At >99.9 Fatigue, the FSM sets PlayerCamera/UseBed.SleepTime to 6 and sends Activate to Player/Sleep.
The global variable named Sanity behaves as an adverse load; its base FSM subtracts 0.05 per second toward zero.
Sanity display begins above 20, warning/effects above 80, mutant spawning above 90, and dying above 95.
In the Sanity dying state, Player Health is reduced by 0.35 per second.
Above Sanity 90, SanityMutantSpawn waits 8..15 seconds and spawns a selected EnemySpawn entry around the player with X/Z offsets -25..25 and Y +5.
Sleep activation applies Fatigue -100, Drunkenness -100, Sanity -30, Hunger +10, Thirst +15, Health +40, and disables weed/alcohol effects.
Player Health is clamped to 0..100; playerDeath fires when Health falls below approximately 0.4.
FallDamage checks GroundTest.fallingTime; after more than 2 seconds it multiplies fallingTime by -9 and routes the value into body-part damage.
Player/InCar tracks InCarInt/InCarBool and switches movement, headbob, footsteps and damage-effect behavior between OnFoot and InCar states.
PlayerCamera/UseFood ray-picks item-related objects within 2 units and reacts to Use input.
SaveLoadGame coordinates save/load, references SaveGame1.es3, world seed, timeline and MapMagic position, and broadcasts save/load-related events.
At +0.01/s, Hunger reaches 100 from 0 in about 166.7 real-time minutes if unmodified.
At +0.02/s, Thirst reaches 100 from 0 in about 83.3 real-time minutes if unmodified.
At +0.02/s, Fatigue reaches 100 from 0 in about 83.3 real-time minutes if unmodified.

title: Floating origin at 1,000 m
statement: NWH.Common.FloatingOrigin sits on the Player with a distance threshold of 1,000 m. It exposes TotalOffset, the sum of all shifts so far.

title: What a shift moves
statement: When the main camera gets 1,000 m from the current origin, FloatingOrigin's LateUpdate translates every root transform in all loaded scenes by the negative camera position. Relative positions are unchanged; absolute world coordinates jump.
guidance: Children of a root, and objects you create as scene roots, move with the world automatically. NPCs, and objects deactivated far away, are roots and are shifted too. Any position cached from an earlier frame (camera, eye, target, bounds) is wrong on the shift frame.

title: Store positions relative to MapMagic
statement: Absolute Unity world coordinates are not stable across shifts. The MapMagic root object is a stable anchor: positions stored relative to it survive any number of shifts.
guidance: Store long-lived positions as offsets from the MapMagic anchor and add Anchor.position on every read. Multi-frame jobs (bakes, paths) must re-read the anchor each step.

title: Registered items switch off beyond 1 km
statement: __GameManager__ :: DeactivateFarAwayItems checks ArrayList_Items every 5 s. Objects more than 1,000 m from the Player are set inactive and are reactivated when the Player comes back within range. Objects on layer 22 (Map) are exempt, and cars are not in this list.
guidance: A deactivated object no longer receives SaveGame and its FSMs restart when it is reactivated.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: names the list, adds reactivation and the layer 22 exemption.

title: Items and cars are destroyed beyond 5 km
statement: DeleteFarAwayItems runs every 10 s and destroys registered items and cars more than 5,000 m from the Player, including all their children: attached parts, cargo locked to a bed, seated NPCs. Sandstorms (ArrayList_Sandstorms) are destroyed beyond 50,000 m, and anything that falls below y = -10,000 is destroyed by DeleteFallingItems.
guidance: Anything a mod parents under a car or item is destroyed with it. Caches that hold references to registered objects must tolerate destroyed entries.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: states explicitly that cars are destroyed too.

title: Cars never deactivate, go kinematic beyond 2 km
statement: Cars are not deactivated by distance. Each car's DistanceKinematic FSM makes its Rigidbody kinematic beyond 2,000 m and non-kinematic again inside it. Cars are still destroyed beyond 5,000 m. Between 1 and 2 km a car is active and physical while its registered loose parts and cargo are already deactivated.
guidance: Do not toggle DistanceKinematic on a moving car: re-enabling it restarts it in KinematicOn, which zeroes the car's velocity.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: cars are exempt only from deactivation, not from destruction.

title: Distances are measured from the Player
statement: The deactivation, destruction and kinematic checks use the distance from the Player object. While driving, the Player is parented inside the car, so the distances follow the car. The floating origin, by contrast, follows the main camera.

title: The three registries
statement: NewGO_ArrayList holds three PlayMakerArrayListProxy lists: ArrayList_Items (items, weapons, loose parts, NPCs, corpses), ArrayList_Cars (vehicles and trailers) and ArrayList_Sandstorms.

title: Registration decides saving and culling
statement: Only objects in these lists are saved and distance-culled. Unregistered objects, such as sanity hallucination mobs or mod spawns that were never added, are never saved and never despawned.

title: Clone names are stable identities
statement: Spawners name clones <prefab>(Clone)N, where N comes from the global itemNameID counter. The name is unique and survives save and load, so it can be used as a persistent identity for mod data.

title: Randomize initialises spawned objects
statement: Spawners send the Randomize event to a new object; item FSMs use it to roll contents such as ammo counts (6 to 12 rounds in an ammo box).
guidance: Disable the object's Randomize FSM if a mod needs to set those values itself.

title: Save-compatible spawn recipe
statement: The vanilla spawn sequence is: instantiate, increment itemNameID, rename to <prefab>(Clone)N, add to the right list once, optionally send Randomize. Adding the same object to a list twice duplicates it on the next load.
guidance: Remove a mod object by dropping it and all its descendants from every list, then destroying it.

title: Inactive objects miss SaveGame
statement: Inactive GameObjects do not receive the game's SaveGame event, so their FSM state is not written.
guidance: Hide objects that must still be saved by disabling renderers and colliders, not with SetActive(false).

title: ES3 saves components on saved roots
statement: ES3 serialises the components on the root of each saved object, including components a mod added at runtime. Children such as an item's Light are not saved.
guidance: Keep mod state in sidecar files rather than components on saved objects; a save carrying mod components can fail to load without the mod.

title: Only referenced car children are saved
statement: A car is saved as its root object plus the children its own FSMs reference (for example Fuel, hinge_exhaust). Children a mod adds at runtime are not saved.

title: The world reappears over several seconds
statement: After a load, saved NPCs, items and a worn backpack are restored progressively over several seconds. In the same period MapMagic regenerates terrain and points of interest (camps, buildings, caves) from the world seed; points of interest are not stored in the save.
guidance: Use grace periods and retries after a load (NPCAI waits up to 20 s in 0.5 s steps) and never cache a 'not found' result permanently.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: points of interest are regenerated, not loaded from the save.

title: Easy Save 3, plain JSON slots
statement: Saves use Easy Save 3. Slots are SaveGameN.es3 (plain JSON) in %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\SawyerK Games\Apocalypter\; slot timestamps are in SaveSettings.es3.

title: Saves go through an in-memory cache
statement: ES3's default location is Cache: the game writes the whole save into memory, and the cache is flushed to the slot file at the end of the save sequence. Changes written directly to the file before that flush are overwritten.

title: The active slot
statement: ES3Settings.defaultSettings.path identifies the active save slot during normal play. The slot buttons set it through ES3SettingsMod.SetSavePath.

title: The slot path is unreliable during a load
statement: While a save is loading, the active path can be empty or still point to the previous slot.
guidance: Record the slot when saving and check it again after the load completes.

title: FSM SaveFile variables are stale
statement: FSM variables such as SaveFile on SaveLoadGame and NewGO_ArrayList are only updated on load and can point to another slot (one showed SaveGame1 while slot 10 was loading).

title: SaveLoadGame state sequence
statement: Save: SaveGame event, wait, SaveGame, back to isPlay. Load: LoadGame, generateTerrain 2, LoadVar, loaded, terrain wait, isPlay. New game: Start, setSeed, generateTerrain, isPlay. A load from the main menu can skip Start.
guidance: Reset per-game mod state on Start, setSeed and LoadGame. Restore mod state about 0.5 s after isPlay following a load.

title: When mod data can be written
statement: Save_NewGO_ArrayList flushes the cache in its state store cached file. Mod data is safe if it is written into the cache before that flush, or to the file (and cache) about 1 s after SaveLoadGame returns to isPlay.

title: ES3.Load overload trap
statement: ES3.Load<string>(key, "", settings) binds to the overload (key, filePath, settings) and reads a file named "". Use ES3.Load<T>(key, settings).

title: Gameplay is PlayMaker
statement: Almost all gameplay logic is PlayMaker FSMs: 1,357 of the 1,947 types in Assembly-CSharp are PlayMaker actions. The remaining C# is asset-store code (Easy Save 3, NWH Vehicle Physics 2, MapMagic, sky, input and sensor libraries).
guidance: Mods read the FSMs, then drive them with SendEvent, Fsm.SetState, FSM variables, or Harmony patches on PlayMaker action classes.

title: FSMs restart on re-enable
statement: Fsm.RestartOnEnable defaults to true, so any FSM whose GameObject or component is re-enabled starts again from its start state.
guidance: Set RestartOnEnable = false before toggling an object you need to resume in place, and restore it afterwards.

title: Third-person camera restarts PlayerCamera FSMs
statement: Switching to the third-person car camera disables the whole PlayerCamera hierarchy, so every FSM under it restarts when the camera comes back.

title: CheckTag detaches parts on restart
statement: Vehicle parts and some held items (cassettes, radios, headlights) start in a CheckTag state that unparents the object and adds a Rigidbody. A restart therefore makes parts fall off cars and throws held items out of the hand; the log shows "Can't add component 'Rigidbody'".
guidance: Set RestartOnEnable = false on CheckTag and LockPhysics while a mod holds the object.

title: FSMs run while paused
statement: PlayMaker FSMs keep running when Time.timeScale is 0, so button and mouse polls still fire in the pause menu. For example, clicking a menu button drops the held item.

title: Gameplay reads legacy input
statement: Gameplay FSMs poll legacy Input Manager buttons through PlayMaker GetButtonDown. The in-game Controls screen rebinds InsaneSystems InputController actions; the legacy axes keep their defaults.
guidance: To suppress a game action, prefix GetButtonDown.OnUpdate, filtered by FSM name and button name.

title: Input button names
statement: Buttons read by the FSMs include Use, Weapon 1/2/3, Weapon off, Drop Weapon, Reload, Jump, Kick, Horn, Use Bandage, Use First Aid, Rotate Item, Change Camera and Adjust-*.

title: Hard-coded function keys
statement: F2 heals, F9 hides the UI and F11 toggles God mode. These keys are not listed in the Controls screen.
guidance: Default mod hotkeys to none or to a key verified to be free.

title: God mode is noclip, not invulnerability
statement: F11 God mode disables collision, gravity and movement FSMs and moves the player to layer 5 (UI). NPCs miss the player only because their sensors do not include that layer; Health is unchanged.

title: FSM lookup traps
statement: FsmVariables.GetFsmInt(name) and the other GetFsm* methods return a new placeholder variable when the name does not exist, so they cannot test for existence. PlayMakerFSM.FindFsmOnGameObject logs a warning for every miss.
guidance: Use the Find* variable methods, iterate GetComponents<PlayMakerFSM>() matching FsmName, and check Fsm.Initialized before reading states.

title: Queries hit triggers and backfaces
statement: The project sets Physics.queriesHitTriggers = true and Physics.queriesHitBackfaces = true.

title: Raycasts hit trigger colliders
statement: Because of that setting, raycasts hit trigger colliders, including the Player's and NPCs' head triggers.

title: Head triggers double damage
statement: Human NPCs carry a trigger capsule on mixamorig:Head with its own Bodypart FSM, which doubles the damage it receives.

title: detectCollisions hides objects from raycasts
statement: Setting Rigidbody.detectCollisions = false also hides the object's colliders from raycasts.
guidance: To make an object non-solid but still hittable, set its colliders to isTrigger instead.

title: detectCollisions is saved
statement: ES3 saves detectCollisions with the object, so a value a mod leaves behind persists across loads.
guidance: Never change detectCollisions on objects the game saves.

title: ClosestPoint fails on non-convex meshes
statement: Collider.ClosestPoint returns the input point unchanged for non-convex MeshColliders. Only Box, Sphere, Capsule and convex Mesh colliders are supported.
guidance: Use Physics.ComputePenetration or ClosestPointOnBounds instead.

title: ClosestPoint fails on terrain
statement: Collider.ClosestPoint also returns the input point unchanged for TerrainColliders.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: observed behaviour, not a possibility.

title: Overlap tests miss enclosed volumes
statement: Overlap tests such as CheckCapsule and OverlapCapsule against a non-convex MeshCollider detect only intersections with its triangles. A capsule wholly inside the rock reads as free.
guidance: To test whether a point is inside solid geometry, raycast upward with backface hits enabled; any hit means the point is enclosed.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: observed on non-convex MeshColliders only, not on terrain.

title: One hit per collider
statement: Physics.RaycastAll and RaycastNonAlloc return at most one hit per collider. A cave built from one mesh collider returns only its roof.
guidance: To find every surface along a ray, repeat single raycasts starting just past each hit.
revision: 2026-10-13: Clarified: standard Unity behaviour, not specific to this game.

title: Sweeps ignore starting overlaps
statement: Sweep queries (SphereCast, CapsuleCast) ignore colliders that already overlap the shape at its starting position.
guidance: Run an overlap test at the start position first to find what the body is already touching.
revision: 2026-10-13: Clarified: standard Unity behaviour, not specific to this game.

title: No NavMesh
statement: Vanilla NPCs do not use a baked Unity NavMesh, and the game ships none.

title: Vanilla chase is a random walk
statement: NPCs chase by running forward while a Rotate FSM turns them randomly and bumper raycasts (layers 0, 8, 11 and 16, without Ground) steer them off obstacles. Idle NPCs stand still; nothing makes them wander.

title: AIModule is available
statement: UnityEngine.AIModule.dll ships with the game, so a mod can bake a NavMesh at runtime.

title: The Player rides inside the car
statement: While driving, the Player object is parented at <car>/DriveTrigger/sitPos/Player.
guidance: Find the Player by name, not by assuming it is a scene root.

title: Seated NPCs belong to the car
statement: NPCs seated in a vehicle are its descendants, so their transform.root is the car.

title: Finding the NPC that owns a collider
statement: A creature root (human or animal) carries a Health FSM, and its body parts carry Bodypart FSMs that add damage to it. The Player also has a Health FSM, and corpses (<Name>_Dead) have Bodypart FSMs but no Health.
guidance: Walk up from the hit collider to the first object with a Health FSM, and stop at a vehicle boundary.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: notes that the Player also has Health and corpses do not.

title: Recognising vehicle boundaries
statement: Attached vehicle parts are tagged vehPart (layer 8); detached parts are tagged vehPartRemoved (layer 9). A vehicle root has an NWH VehicleController component.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: vehPart is a tag, not an object name.

title: The game destroys the plugin's own GameObject
statement: On scene load the game destroys the BepInEx plugin's GameObject, even though BepInEx marks it DontDestroyOnLoad. As a result BaseUnityPlugin.Update, LateUpdate and OnGUI never run, and Chainloader.PluginInfos[guid].Instance reads as a destroyed object.
guidance: Run per-frame logic on a separate hidden GameObject (HideAndDontSave plus DontDestroyOnLoad), recreate it on SceneManager.sceneLoaded, and re-find game references after every load. Test plugin presence with ReferenceEquals(info.Instance, null).
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: the trap is the plugin's own persistent object, not ordinary scene objects.

title: Undo your own changes before the game takes over
statement: Vanilla release paths only restore what vanilla changed. When the game drops a weapon or releases an item, it re-enables what it disabled itself; colliders, gravity or renderers a mod switched off stay off, and the object can fall through the terrain.
guidance: Before handing an object back to a vanilla FSM, restore every change the mod made to it.
revision: 2026-10-13: Corrected: the earlier wording reversed who must clean up.

title: Plugin versions must be plain numbers
statement: BepInEx parses the [BepInPlugin] version as System.Version. A version like 1.2.0-beta makes it skip the plugin silently.
guidance: Use plain versions such as 1.2.0. If a mod is missing from the load list, check its version first.

title: Parse numbers with the invariant culture
statement: Players run the game with comma-decimal locales. Float parsing or formatting with the current culture threw exceptions at startup for French, Russian, Polish and Portuguese players and misread values for German ones.
guidance: Use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture for every number you parse or format yourself.

title: JsonUtility drops nested arrays
statement: Unity JsonUtility in a BepInEx plugin silently drops arrays of nested custom [Serializable] classes; plain string[] survives.
guidance: Use a small hand-written JSON serializer and check the written output.
